title: I’m scared to finally show people the game I’ve spent 7 years making
author: mutantcivil
selftext:
Hi everyone. I’ve been working on my game on and off for almost 7 years, and I’m finally at the point where it’s about 99% done.  
But now that I’m ready to put out a Steam page and release a demo, I’ve started feeling strangely hesitant.  
It’s not that I think the game is bad. I just keep thinking: *What if people don’t like it? What if nobody cares?*  
There isn’t really an audience waiting for this game, so putting it out there suddenly feels much more intimidating than actually making it.  
Has anyone else felt this way after spending years on a game? How did you get yourself to finally hit “publish”?

comments.author: msfs_piolot
comments.body: just do it

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Yeah, i know. I think I just need to stop overthinking it and actually hit publish. Thanks!

replies.author: Vividds
replies.body: I don't know if this help, but there's a saying that maybe will boost your CONFIDENCE like "You won’t know how to walk unless you learn how to fall."

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Hey man. Thank you so much for revisiting. I have not published it yet but i did updated my web page dor my game. I will make sure to publish it in next 1-2 days. Everything else is done.

comments.author: derAres
comments.body: Maybe you should ask in indie game dev or something, because you're in aigamedev and ai has been barely good enough to help with games for a year or two max.

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Yeah. Thanks. I will ask there as well.

comments.author: [deleted]
comments.body: [removed]

comments.author: rhinoceros100
comments.body:
if you don't post it, its guaranteed to not be liked or cared about.  

I just posted mine(www.chiefairlineofficer.com) in this same community today and received great feedback

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Wow. Thats real great. Yeah I am going to do it. Feeling a little pumped now. 😅

replies.author: Jackker
replies.body:
For some reason, your website hammers my laptop (ThinkPad P1G2 with 64GB Ram). 

From the instant I load it, my laptop fan spins up and the website gets incredibly sluggish. I wonder if it's due to the background animation.

Otherwise, the game sounds really cool!

replies.author: Hungry-Boysenberry98
replies.body: I experieced this same sluggish behaviour on Samsung s24+ when visiting your site.

comments.author: ImpressiveFocus303
comments.body: 7 years of working on game? In isolation? I hope it's only a hobby project and you are willing accept that you'll make $0 out of it (ignoring opportunity costs).

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Yeah, I think this is the scariest part. I honestly don’t know what I’d do if I stopped making games. I had a hit game a few years ago, but ever since then, I’ve been struggling to find the courage to release something again. I guess I’m just scared that this one won’t live up to what I did before.

replies.author: Lord-Fondlemaid
replies.body: What was the hit game if you don't mind me asking?

comments.author: StrongCucumber
comments.body: Is it the game in your post history? Looks very nice to me

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Yes, it is! Thanks for the compliment. And yeah, it plays pretty well too. Let’s see how it goes. I’ll release a free demo on Steam first, and once it’s ready, I’ll share the link with the community.

replies.author: spiralsammy
replies.body: Following for demo release details when they drop

comments.author: BoltVnderhuge
comments.body: Post it, it will get destroyed, then you’ll improve it from the feedback and have something beautiful!

comments.author: mutantcivil
comments.body: Wow, thats exactly what i am hoping for! 😄 I guess I just need to put it out there and let the feedback do its thing. Thanks for the push

replies.author: ctimmermans
replies.body: Looks great from your post history. Where's the download? :-)

comments.author: davidhampshire
comments.body: Do it dude I'd love to see

replies.author: mutantcivil
replies.body: Thabks mate. I will beat my fear of failure and will release my demo asap.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I have a game I've been working on for 10 months now and I'm still nervous to show what I've created thus far but I really been meaning to make a trailer for it hopefully soon. I have the same anxiety you do and especially with how strong anti-sentiment is lately I've just been very unwilling to present it

comments.author: ExtremeCenterism
comments.body: This is part of the reason they say "as soon as you have something to post, post it"

comments.author: Vortex_Voider
comments.body: this is perfectly natural, posting it to the public is the most vulnerable thing you can do after so much effort

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Beta test it. Show it to dozens of people first.

comments.author: loopywolf
comments.body: We'll support you

comments.author: Droopy0093
comments.body: OP I have doubts you have been working on a game for 7 years. Based on your post history you have produced a couple AI assisted games which is find so in this case I feel like you are lying in order to trick people into thinking you manually created all the code and assets for a game. Can you share the proof from 7 years ago where your work started? I am certainly curious to see where the starting points were.

comments.author: Officialpolygrafix
comments.body: Yes, that anxiety you're feeling is perfectly natural, and probably even more so after working on a project for 7 years.  It's ok to let it go into the wild so now you can focus on the most difficult part of this journey, marketing your game.

comments.author: luciddream00
comments.body: It's always a bit agonizing to put something you care about into the world like that, but you didn't spend 7 years on it just to keep it to yourself. Maybe it does well, maybe it doesn't but having a finished game will help whatever you do next.

comments.author: Hour-Eleven
comments.body:
If people don’t like it, take a breath, and either make some changes or start the next project!

Good luck, friend!

comments.author: msew
comments.body:
I would be interested in what the 7 years were comprised of.

Like a break down of: 

-Human effort

-AI effort

And what did that AI effort do to allow you to ship.

comments.author: AetherAndEntropy
comments.body: Did you make it for other people or yourself?

comments.author: ElectricalPickle2137
comments.body: Don't release it and you'll never be a failure. Isn't that what you're fighting about?

comments.author: ctimmermans
comments.body: Minimize regret in life

comments.author: InsensitiveClown
comments.body:
Well, I'll tell you: some people will hate it, some will write shitty thing, while others will love it, praise you and throw you money.
Amongst all of these, a few will have the integrity, courtesy, moral fortitude to tell you their honest, constructive, thoughts, helping you to progress and improve your game, and yourself. For this reason alone, publishing your work, whatever that work is, is imperative. Because you grow and become a better professional with it, and a better human.

comments.author: AdCommon2138
comments.body: Damn, bro had ai tools making his game since 2019

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body: hey mate, go for it. a game lives through its players. its not a game till someone plays it.

comments.author: telemes34
comments.body: Bro just stop trusting your inner voice is just your brain estimating the future. Ignore it and you will be fine. Worry about the future is not going to fix the future is going to mess up today's coffee! 🤣

comments.author: Melodic_Charity_1770
comments.body:
Don't be afraid to launch, unlaunch and relaunch your game. Expecting traffic and success in this crazy economy for attention right away is not sensible. 

Marketing, promoting and sharing your game will take months and months of slow work. You have finished the game, but a whole phase of work has just begun.

comments.author: EllvanStudios
comments.body: You gotta just take that leap. It won't diminish your efforts over this time and you can celebrate having built something and worked on it for so long!

comments.author: Hans_Sandblom
comments.body: Kör på, jag var livrädd attxsläppa min seo bok, även den inte 100, man måste släppa rädslan. Kör på, blir magiskt

comments.author: emperormarkus
comments.body: I think you just have to go for it. I am actually less worried about random people online hating my games than people who really know me. Whatever the outcome you will feel good you have done something few other people have. Also publishing will pave the way for doing the next one. Is a great journey. Good luck.
